Guiding Case No. 267

A Cultural Media Co., Ltd. v. You — enforcement implementation case

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on August 28, 2025)

Keywords

enforcement; enforcement implementation; online platform account; delivery of account and password; change of real-name authentication information

Key Points for Enforcement Implementation

In the enforcement of delivery of an online platform account and password, full consideration shall be given to the characteristics of online platform accounts. In accordance with the real-name authentication and other requirements stipulated by law, the relevant real-name authentication information shall be changed in accordance with the law at the same time as the account and password are delivered. Where the enforcement respondent fails to perform the aforementioned obligations, the enforcement applicant may apply to the enforcement court for issuance of a notice of assistance in enforcement, requesting the relevant online platform to change the real-name authentication information.

Basic Facts

A Cultural Media Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as A Media Company) filed a lawsuit on the ground of a dispute over unfair competition, requesting the court to confirm that an account on a certain platform named "Lang Mou Xian" belonged to A Media Company, and to order You and others to deliver the account and password to A Media Company; and to order You and others to cease the unfair competition acts and to compensate economic losses of RMB 6.18 million. The Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court rendered civil judgment (2020) Yu 01 Min Chu No. 1035 on June 29, 2022, confirming that the account named "Lang Mou Xian" on a certain platform belonged to A Media Company, ordering You to deliver the aforesaid platform account and password to A Media Company within three days after the judgment took effect, and dismissing A Media Company's other claims including the claim for compensation of economic losses of RMB 6.18 million from You and others. After the judgment was pronounced, A Media Company appealed. The Chongqing High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2022) Yu Min Zhong No. 859 on December 26, 2022, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

After the aforesaid judgment took effect, as You failed to perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument, A Media Company applied to the Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court for compulsory enforcement. A Media Company requested the enforcement court to issue a notice of assistance in enforcement to the operator of the platform, A Technology Co., Ltd. and others, requesting the aforementioned companies to assist in clearing the original real-name authentication information of the account involved in the case, re-authenticating it with the identity information of A Media Company, and unbinding the originally bound mobile phone number and rebinding it with a mobile phone number designated by A Media Company. It was also found that You had been in custody since September 18, 2022 due to involvement in a criminal case, and was later sentenced to eight years' imprisonment for the crime of embezzlement.

On March 24, 2023, the Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court rendered enforcement ruling (2023) Yu 01 Zhi No. 164, clearing the real-name authentication information of You in the platform account named "Lang Mou Xian", unbinding the originally bound mobile phone number of the account and rebinding it with the mobile phone number designated by A Media Company. After the ruling took effect, in accordance with the requirements of the enforcement ruling and the notice of assistance in enforcement, the aforementioned online platform operating company assisted A Media Company in completing the change of the login password, real-name authentication information, and registered mobile phone number of the account involved.

Enforcement Result

On April 27, 2023, the Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court issued case closure notice (2023) Yu 01 Zhi No. 164, and the enforcement of this case was completed.

Reasoning

The focus of the dispute in the trial stage of this case involved the ownership of the account. The effective judgment determined that the rights to the account belonged to A Media Company, and the judgment item stated delivery of the account and password. According to the facts found and the reasons determined in the judgment, the account was decided to be registered by A Media Company. Because an enterprise applying for registration and authentication of an account must first register using a mobile phone number, A Media Company had You, then the legal representative of the company, use her mobile phone number to register, and You managed the account on behalf of the company. According to the content of the delivery of rights to the account confirmed by the effective judgment, it should be the complete delivery of all user permissions, rights and interests of the account to A Media Company. Therefore, the key to delivery of the account and password is that A Media Company exercises the rights to the account, achieving lawful possession, independent control, and operation, use, and management of the account.

Online platform accounts are highly dependent on real-name authentication and verification of registered mobile phone numbers, including real-name information of the registered identity, mobile phone number, etc. If the aforementioned complete elements are lacking, and only the account and password are possessed, then others who hold the registration information can still reset the account and password using the registered real-name information, mobile phone number, etc., affecting the right of the lawful owner to lawfully possess, control, and dominate the relevant account. In this case, if You only delivered the login account and password without clearing her real-name information and changing the mobile phone number, although A Media Company could log in using the password and use and manage the account, You could still reset the account and password through her identity information and mobile phone number. A Media Company would also find it difficult to implement matters such as account management, backend operation, and data migration due to the lack of verification of registered user identity and mobile phone number. Thus, delivery of only the account and password cannot fully vest the rights to the account in A Media Company. Moreover, if others illegally use the account to engage in illegal activities, it would make it difficult to verify the identity of the actor, harming public interest. Therefore, the core content of the delivery of the account should be changing it to A Media Company's registered user identity and mobile phone number, etc.

Article 24, paragraph 1 of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "When network operators provide users with network access, domain name registration services, handle network access procedures for fixed telephones, mobile telephones, etc., or provide users with services such as information publication and instant messaging, they shall require users to provide true identity information when signing agreements with users or confirming service provision. If users do not provide true identity information, network operators shall not provide relevant services to them." Under normal circumstances, changing the subject information of an online platform account should follow relevant regulations, including procedures such as submitting an application to the platform, the platform conducting authentication and verification, and publicizing the change of subject information. However, the enforcement respondent You objectively had obstacles to performance. Therefore, the enforcement court, based on the application of the enforcement applicant A Media Company, completed the change of the real-name identity information of the account involved by notifying the relevant platform to assist in enforcement.

Relevant Laws

Article 24 of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China
Article 263 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Article 259 of the 2021 Amendment of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China applied in this case)
